articles.title: How I Built a Peptide Dosage Calculator with Next.js — and Why SSR Matters More Than You Think
articles.excerpt: A researcher spends 30 seconds doing peptide math before every injection. I built a tool that does it instantly. Here's the surprising thing I learned: for a calculator tool, SSR isn't about performan…
articles.body: A researcher spends 30 seconds doing peptide math before every injection. I built a tool that does it instantly. Here's the surprising thing I learned: for a calculator tool, SSR isn't about performance — it's about whether Google even knows your calculator exists. The Problem I Was Solving If you're not familiar with peptide research: researchers reconstitute lyophilized (freeze-dried) peptides by adding bacteriostatic water, then draw specific doses into insulin syringes. The math isn't hard — it's just annoying: "I have a 10mg vial, added 2ml of water, I need 250mcg per dose — how many units on a 0.3ml syringe?" "I'm running BPC-157 and TB-500 together, different vials, different doses — what are my draw volumes?" Most researchers use Excel or a notepad.
articles.author: Jamin

articles.title: The Best Approach to Dependency Vulnerability Scanning in CI Pipelines
articles.excerpt: The Best Approach to Dependency Vulnerability Scanning in CI Pipelines Dependency vulnerabilities are the silent killers of modern software projects. A single outdated package can expose your entire a…
articles.body: The Best Approach to Dependency Vulnerability Scanning in CI Pipelines Dependency vulnerabilities are the silent killers of modern software projects. A single outdated package can expose your entire application to attacks, and with the average project pulling in hundreds of transitive dependencies, manual tracking is impossible. After years of implementing security scanning across Python, TypeScript, and React projects, I've learned that the "best" approach isn't about choosing a single tool—it's about building a multi-layered strategy that catches vulnerabilities early, fails fast when necessary, and doesn't bring your development velocity to a grinding halt. Let's cut through the noise and build a practical scanning strategy.
articles.author: BMarsaw

articles.excerpt: Running Claude Code in a Sandboxed Docker Container If you've ever wanted to run Claude Code with full permissions, without worrying about it touching anything outside your project. This one-liner ins…
articles.body: Running Claude Code in a Sandboxed Docker Container If you've ever wanted to run Claude Code with full permissions, without worrying about it touching anything outside your project. This one-liner install script does exactly that. The script builds a minimal Docker image ( node:22-slim ) with Claude Code and the rtk CLI pre-installed, then wires up two shell aliases: claude-docker — launches Claude Code inside the container with --dangerously-skip-permissions , your current directory mounted at /workspace claude-docker-sh — drops you into a bash shell in the same container, useful for poking around or debugging Because everything runs inside the container, "skip permissions" mode is much less risky than running it on your bare host — Claude can act freely, but it's boxed into the container…

articles.title: The JavaScript Gamepad API: A Practical Guide to Reading Controller Input
articles.excerpt: The first time you wire up a game controller in a browser, the API will almost certainly appear broken. You plug in an Xbox pad, call navigator.getGamepads(), and get back an array of four null values…
articles.body: The first time you wire up a game controller in a browser, the API will almost certainly appear broken. You plug in an Xbox pad, call navigator.getGamepads() , and get back an array of four null values. Nothing is wrong. The API is just quieter and stranger than most browser APIs, and almost none of that strangeness is obvious from the method signature. This is a walkthrough of how the Gamepad API actually behaves: how polling works, what buttons and axes really contain, why dead zones exist, and why the same controller reports different data over USB than over Bluetooth. There is working code for each part, and a section at the end on the mistakes that cost me the most time. Browser-based controller testing is worth understanding for two separate reasons.

articles.title: Beyond the Snapshot: Integrating 30-Day Environmental Intelligence into AI Agents
articles.excerpt: I've been watching people build AI agents that are incredibly good at refactoring TypeScript, but completely blind to the physical world they inhabit. You can give an agent access to your GitHub, your…
articles.body: I've been watching people build AI agents that are incredibly good at refactoring TypeScript, but completely blind to the physical world they inhabit. You can give an agent access to your GitHub, your Jira, and your AWS console, yet as soon as you ask it how local air quality might affect a planned outdoor event in San Francisco, it starts hallucinating or giving generic advice based on training data from two years ago. The problem isn't the LLM's reasoning; it's the lack of a real-time, high-fidelity environmental sensor via MCP. Most developers solve this by trying to wrap a raw API—in this case, Google’s Air Quality API—into their own custom server.

articles.excerpt: Marvel has made Black Panther 3 official, and confirmed it will launch on December 15, 2028.
articles.body: Marvel has made Black Panther 3 official, and confirmed it will launch on December 15, 2028. Details of Ryan Coogler's upcoming threequel were confirmed today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance. Notably, British actor David Jonsson was announced as starring in the film as the son of T'Challa, previously seen as a child in Black Panther: Wakanda Forever. Jonsson previously appeared in Alien: Romulus and The Long Walk. Letitia Wright will return as Shuri, while Winston Duke will reprise his role as M'Baku. So both of them presumably survive Avengers: Secret Wars, then. For a movie that Marvel had previously not officially confirmed, we actually did know a fair bit about the project before today.

articles.body: Ryan Reynolds and Hayley Atwell will reprise their Marvel roles as Deadpool and Peggy Carter in Avengers: Doomsday , it's been confirmed. Both actors appeared on stage today at San Diego Comic Con during Marvel's announcement panel in Hall H, where IGN was in attendance. Deadpool now wears a grey suit, which Reynolds referred to as his "Canadian tuxedo." "Longtime listener, first time caller," Reynolds said, in character as Deadpool, dropping in on the Marvel panel. "I'm a huge fan. I’m not wearing a Doom mask over this mask because I don’t want to ruin the lines of my Canadian tuxedo," he continued, referencing the plastic Doctor Doom masks handed out to everyone in the audience.

articles.title: An off-the-shelf camera could help us find more black holes smashing together
articles.excerpt: "It doesn't require any new technology development, which is almost unheard of for solving a LIGO instrumentation problem."
articles.body: Fixing a problem inside one of the world's most sophisticated scientific observatories might seem like the kind of challenge that demands a multimillion-dollar upgrade or revolutionary new technology. But for scientists working on the Laser Interferometer Gravitational-Wave Observatory ( LIGO ), which listens for ripples in spacetime generated by cosmic collisions like merging black holes , the solution to a mild but persistent engineering challenge turns out to be as simple as an off-the-shelf camera.

articles.title: NASA astronaut, 2 cosmonauts returning to Earth on July 26: Watch it live
articles.excerpt: NASA astronaut Chris Williams and two Russian cosmonauts will return to Earth from the International Space Station early Sunday morning (July 26), and you can watch their homecoming live.
articles.body: A U.S.-Russian crew will return to Earth from the International Space Station early Sunday morning (July 26), and you can watch their homecoming live. A Soyuz spacecraft carrying NASA astronaut Chris Williams and Sergey Kud-Sverchkov and Sergei Mikaev of the Russian space agency Roscosmos is scheduled to undock from the orbiting lab on Sunday at 3:02 a.m. EDT (0702 GMT). The Soyuz, known as MS-28, will land on the steppe of Kazakhstan about 3.5 hours later, at 6:26 a.m. EDT (1026 GMT). You can watch these milestones here at Space.com, courtesy of NASA. Russia's Soyuz MS-28 spacecraft is seen docked to the International Space Station shortly after its arrival on Nov. 27, 2026. (Image credit: NASA) The coverage starts today (July 25) at 9:40 a.m.

articles.title: SpaceX's Starship megarocket makes the 'softest splashdown' ever after launching next-gen Starlink satellites in Flight 13 test (video)
articles.excerpt: SpaceX launched Starship, the world's most powerful rocket, on a critical 13th test flight on July 24, a stunning test flight that notched big success and ended with a huge surprise.
articles.body: SpaceX launched the world's most powerful rocket on a critical 13th test flight late Friday, but there was no triskaidekaphobia on this mission. The July 24 test launch, Space's Starship Flight 13 mission , sent a towering rocket the size of a 40-story skyscraper into space from South Texas, returned its massive Booster to Earth, and then — in a feat perhaps none saw coming — gently landed its Starship upper stage in the Indian Ocean, where it tipped over to float belly up on the sea. "Starship is intact, floating in the ocean and transmitting telemetry!" SpaceX CEO Elon Musk wrote on X . SpaceX's Starship Flight 13 test flight lifts off from Starbase, Texas on July 24, 2026.
